discovery: Arrays of individually trapped neutral atoms entangled through Rydberg blockade, for quantum simulation and computation

nominees.name: Antoine Browaeys
nominees.affiliation: Institut d'Optique Graduate School, Université Paris-Saclay, CNRS, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum optics
motivation: These physicists turned single neutral atoms into fully controlled quantum objects and made them interact on demand. Lukin co-proposed the Rydberg dipole blockade as a mechanism for entangling neutral atoms. In 2009 the groups of Saffman and of Browaeys (working with Grangier) independently demonstrated the blockade between two atoms held in optical tweezers, and they then used it to produce entanglement and quantum gates. Building on this, they assembled defect-free, reconfigurable arrays of hundreds of atoms. These arrays have been used to observe quantum magnetism, quantum phase transitions, topological spin liquids and error-corrected logical qubits. The work started from a fundamental question: can one control and entangle single atoms one by one? It has since become a leading platform for the second quantum revolution in quantum simulation and computing. It is a clear example of elegant quantum optics growing into a practical tool.
